Hart was named an assistant coach for the Purdue Fort Wayne women's soccer program on April 1, 2025.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHart was most recently part of Ithaca College women's soccer program as a graduate assistant coach from 2023-2024.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe Bombers had an exceptional 2024 season, finishing 14-3-4. Ithaca finished first in the Liberty League, earning the top seed in the Liberty League tournament for the first time in program history. The Bombers were the best defensive team in the league, recording the least goals allowed (0.37 goals per game). Following the conclusion of the regular-season, Ithaca was 11th nationally in shutout percentage (14 shutouts, .737), 13th in goals against average (.364), and 14th in save percentage (.883). They earned a season-high #8 ranking in the October 22 United Soccer Coaches National Poll. The Bombers won their second Liberty League Tournament title in three years, capturing the league’s automatic bid to the NCAA Tournament. The NCAA berth marked the program’s 30th appearance in the Division III Tournament, where the Bombers advanced to the second round. The coaching staff was named the Liberty League Coaching Staff of the Year following the 2024 season. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2023, the Bombers finished the year with a 10-3-4 overall record, finishing third in the Liberty League. During her time at Ithaca, Hart's players earned six All-Region selections, 15 players on the All-Liberty League Team, and 39 players on the League All-Academic team.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHart earned her master’s degree in exercise sport science with a concentration in mental performance from Ithaca College in December 2024.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHart played collegiate soccer at the University of Wisconsin-La Crosse. She appeared in 58 games with 24 starts, recording 5 goals and 6 assists. UWL earned two bids to the NCAA Division III Tournament during Hart’s tenure. The Eagles appeared in the quarterfinal match in 2021 and finished in the Sweet 16 in 2022. In Hart’s final season at UWL, the Eagles finished with their best record in program history (21-2-1). UWL finished undefeated in conference play, winning both the WIAC regular-season and conference tournament titles. Hart was a three-time WIAC Scholastic Honor Roll recipient. Hart received her bachelor’s degree in psychology with a minor in sociology from UW-La Crosse in 2022.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHart served as the assistant varsity soccer coach at Central High School in La Crosse in 2021 and 2022. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHart was the head coach for the U19 girls at Syracuse Development Academy from 2024-2025, competing in the Girls Academy League. She is originally from Sun Prairie,
